The Web of Babel

A browser for an internet imagined by an AI
"The certainty that everything has already been written annuls us, or renders us phantasmal."
— Jorge Luis Borges, The Library of Babel

In Borges' story, the Library of Babel contains every possible book. Every possible book has a unique location in the library. You know the location, you know the book.

The Web of Babel is the same idea, applied to the Web through the magic of large language models. Given an LLM, every possible web page can be generated — in a lossy way. All we need to know is where in the Web of Babel that web page can be found. And since web pages have addresses known as URLs, we already know.

So this browser lets you visit the mind of an LLM by web address. Just type a URL in the location bar. You can visit Lonely Planet's guide to Berlin and get decent advice. Or check for the latest tech news on Hacker News — click any of the posts and it will show what the AI thinks the underlying article looks like. The Web of Babel of course comes with a working Google search engine to search for anything you'd want. Geocities might have been taken down, but it still exists here for all your crystal needs. You can browse past news sites from before they — or indeed the web — were a thing, like this BBC report of the battle of Waterloo. You can of course also visit this page itself on the Web of Babel and see what an AI thinks it should look like.

Getting started

Click Options in the menu bar to configure your AI provider. You'll need an API key from one of the supported providers:

  • Google Gemini — free API key at aistudio.google.com
  • OpenRouter — many free models available
  • Anthropic or OpenAI — requires a paid API key
  • Ollama — run models locally, no key needed

Bookmarks

The Bookmarks menu comes with a few pre-generated pages you can browse immediately, even without an API key. These are cached snapshots. Click the cached badge in the location bar to regenerate any page fresh. You can bookmark any page you visit, and its content will be saved so you can revisit it instantly.

Tips

  • Follow links and watch the hallucination compound
  • View Source shows the raw generated HTML
  • Save Page downloads the current page as an HTML file
  • The Back button shows cached pages instantly
  • Try real URLs, historical URLs, or completely made-up ones

The Web of Babel is a project by Douwe Osinga.
